subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` configured-model health check, or should this behavior be folded into fallback-chain testing or staged model-migration UX instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a live all-model probe creates a new CLI contract with token/rate-limit cost, output semantics, auth-profile handling, and overlap with other model-safety requests.

options.title: Add Opt-In Status Probe
options.body: Implement `models status --probe --all` as the canonical broad configured-model health sweep while keeping default `--probe` behavior unchanged.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback/Migration UX
options.body: Make fallback-chain testing or staged model migration own configured-model validation and keep status probes focused on auth/profile diagnostics.

options.title: Defer New Live Probe Mode
options.body: Keep the issue open for later if maintainers do not want another token-consuming CLI diagnostic yet.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Status Probe
recommendation.body: Implement `models status --probe --all` as the canonical broad configured-model health sweep while keeping default `--probe` behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from prior model-status guidance and recent model status/auth health history.
